text:
elaine: Quick update — ran a full canary of the late-bind-scheduler + hybrid-kv-prefetch stack against a prod-like fleet this morning. TL;DR: p99 latency for short-chat workloads dropped ~14% (220ms -> 190ms) and our cost-per-1M-tokens estimate improved ~9% due to fewer kernel wakeups and better KV cache hit aggregation. :rocket:

samir: Nice! Any surprises or regressions so far?

ana (perf-rd): No correctness regressions in the 72h canary. We did see a minor latency bump for very long-context sessions (>8k tokens) on older CUDA 2.1 boxes — looks like prefetch thrash where concurrent prefetches compete and increase tail latency. Filed PERF-482 with a repro and traces.

matt (eng-latency): Can we add a simple backoff when active_seq_len > 8k and retry the canary? Should be a quick conditional. If that eliminates the thrash we can proceed.

ci-bot: perf-check results attached: baseline vs canary 
- short-chat (avg seq 128): p50 38ms -> 34ms, p95 120ms -> 105ms, p99 220ms -> 190ms
- multi-turn (avg seq 640): p50 120ms -> 108ms, p95 360ms -> 330ms, p99 720ms -> 680ms
- throughput: +6% at stable latency
All unit/e2e tests passed.

elaine: Repro + config for the canary we ran:
```yaml
canary:
  name: late-bind-scheduler-v1
  percentage: 10
  rollout_steps:
    - 10
    - 30
    - 100
  fallback: stable-v3
```
We also enabled per-worker prefetch limits and aggregate KV windowing which cut redundant prefetches in half.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: step 1 (10% traffic) — initial checks green.

samir: Please put a short note in release-notes and add an entry to the console changelog for "Scheduler + KV prefetch: p99 latency and cost improvements". Ops needs flag names for emergency rollback.

ana (perf-rd): Added eval sets: web-chat-100 and long-context-smoke. Also set an alert: p99 > 250ms for short-chat will auto-signal the rollout monitor.

matt (eng-latency): I'll patch the prefetch backoff tomorrow morning and run canary2 (same config but with backoff enabled). If canary2 is green we'll complete a 100% rollout by EOD. Also updating the batcher tuning doc with the new 'kv_prefetch_backoff_ms' knob.

elaine: Plan sounds good. Thanks for the quick triage everyone. Once canary2 is green I'll post a short blurb for all-hands to highlight the cost wins. :party: 

samir: small ask — include a short runbook snippet for rollback (routes to stable-v3) in the console changelog so support can flip it if needed.

elaine: Will do. Closing notes: expect ~9% unit-cost reduction on CPU+GPU mixes for typical chat traffic; savings will vary by model/seq distribution. Tracking PERF-482 for the long-context thrash.

matt (eng-latency): ACK, monitoring dashboards updated.

deploy-bot: Canary step 1 complete — health checks remain green. Next step pending manual approval.
